extracted.intended_audience: USPTO patent examiners, patent owners, third-party requesters, and practitioners involved in ex parte reexamination practice
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance for evaluating and processing requests for ex parte reexamination of U.S. patents, including the legal standard for ordering reexamination, what prior art and claims may be considered, required contents of decisions, and special procedural situations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Time for deciding request
rubrics_metrics.description: The determination of whether or not to reexamine must be made within 3 months following the filing date of a request. See 35 U.S.C. 303(a) and 37 CFR 1.515(a).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If the 3-month period ends on a Saturday, Sunday, or Federal holiday within the District of Columbia, the determination must be mailed by the preceding business day. The examiner should take up a request about 6 weeks after filing and the decision should be mailed within 10 weeks of filing. When reexamination for the same patent is already pending, the examiner should immediately take up the new request (no 6-week delay). A determination to reexamine may be made at any time during the period of enforceability of a patent.

rubrics_metrics.name: Substantial New Question of Patentability (SNQ) — threshold
rubrics_metrics.description: The presence or absence of 'a substantial new question of patentability' determines whether or not reexamination is ordered. If prior art patents and printed publications raise a substantial question of patentability of at least one claim, then a substantial new question of patentability is present, unless the same question has already been decided by a final holding of invalidity or by the Office in a previous examination or pending reexamination.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: SNQ is not defined in the statute and is developed case-by-case. A prior art patent or printed publication raises an SNQ where there is a substantial likelihood that a reasonable examiner would consider it important in deciding patentability. It is not necessary that a 'prima facie' case of unpatentability exist; SNQ may exist even if the examiner would not necessarily reject the claim as anticipated or obvious based on the art.

rubrics_metrics.name: Scope of prior art considered in making SNQ determination
rubrics_metrics.description: The determination may be made 'with or without consideration of other patents or printed publications'—the examiner is not limited to the patents/printed publications relied on in the request.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The examiner can base SNQ on: (a) the prior art relied on in the request; (b) a combination of the prior art in the request and other prior art found elsewhere; or (c) entirely different patents or printed publications. The examiner may also consider patents and publications of record in the patent file and, where appropriate, perform a limited additional search if there is a reasonable likelihood that prior art can be found to supply any deficiency necessary to raise an SNQ.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of 'old art' (previously cited/considered art) as sole basis for SNQ
rubrics_metrics.description: Reliance on previously cited/considered art ('old art') does not necessarily preclude the existence of an SNQ for reexaminations ordered on or after November 2, 2002 (Public Law 107-273).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Determinations must be fact-specific and case-by-case. An SNQ may be based solely on old art where the old art is presented/viewed in a new light or in a different way in view of a material new argument or interpretation. When SNQ is based solely on old art, include form paragraph 22.01.01 in the order and explain how the old art is being applied differently (e.g., examples and bracketed instructions in the form paragraph). This form paragraph is only used the first time the already-cited art is applied.

rubrics_metrics.name: Effect of prior Office decisions (favorable or adverse) on SNQ
rubrics_metrics.description: Prior favorable decisions by the Office on the same or substantially identical prior art in relation to the same patent generally mean an SNQ is not raised; prior adverse decisions by the Office on the same or substantially identical prior art usually indicate an SNQ is present.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examiner should check patent file history to see whether the prior art relied upon was previously cited/considered in an earlier concluded examination (referred to as 'old art'). For determinations after Nov. 2, 2002, prior consideration of art does not automatically preclude SNQ—must analyze whether art is presented in a new light. Prior adverse decisions in reissue or other Office proceedings based on prior art typically support finding an SNQ. Prior favorable Office determinations favorable to patentee based on the same art weigh against SNQ.

rubrics_metrics.name: Effect of federal court decisions on SNQ
rubrics_metrics.description: A final holding of claim invalidity by the courts (after all appeals) is controlling on the Office and precludes SNQ as to those claims; nonfinal judicial holdings are not controlling; final holdings of validity do not necessarily preclude an SNQ because of different standards of proof.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Office will accord some deference to district court factual findings but makes an independent SNQ determination. A final court decision of validity does not necessarily mean no SNQ is present; a final decision of invalidity or unenforceability after all appeals precludes SNQ for the affected claims.

rubrics_metrics.name: Claims considered in deciding request
rubrics_metrics.description: The claims in effect at the time of the determination will be the basis for deciding whether an SNQ is present (37 CFR 1.515(a)).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examiner ordinarily concentrates on the claims for which reexamination is requested, but the finding of SNQ can be based on any claim in the patent. If an SNQ is found as to any claim, reexamination will be ordered and will normally cover all claims except those finally held invalid by a Federal Court decision. Amendments or new claims will not be considered when deciding a request. The decision should discuss all patent claims to inform the patent owner of the examiner’s position.

rubrics_metrics.name: Decision should identify and explain at least one SNQ when granting request
rubrics_metrics.description: If a request is granted, the examiner’s decision must conclude that an SNQ has been raised by identifying all claims/issues, the patents/printed publications relied on, and providing a brief statement of the rationale supporting each new question.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The examiner must identify at least one SNQ and explain how the cited patents/publications raise such a question. The decision should indicate, insofar as possible, the examiner's initial position on issues identified in the request so that the patent owner can respond. In simple cases the examiner may adopt the requester’s reasons. Prior art relied on should be listed on appropriate PTO forms and copies supplied only where not previously supplied. For each SNQ the decision should point out: (A) which prior art adds new teaching as to at least one claim; (B) what that new teaching is; (C) the claims directed to; (D) that the new teaching was not previously considered/addressed in prior examination or final court holding; (F) where relevant, why the reference is available as prior art (date/availability discussion). The decision should not decide claim patentability — only whether SNQ exists.

rubrics_metrics.name: Contents required in a decision denying reexamination
rubrics_metrics.description: If no substantial new question of patentability is found, the examiner should prepare a decision denying the reexamination request and must indicate why for each cited patent and printed publication the citation is inadequate.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use form paragraph 22.02 as introductory paragraph. For each cited reference explain whether it is: (A) cumulative to art already considered; (B) not available against the claims (wrong date or not a publication); (C) not important to a reasonable examiner in deciding patentability even though not cumulative and available; or (D) barred by guidelines (e.g., previously considered in earlier concluded examination). The examiner should also respond to the substance of each requester argument based on patents/printed publications. Arguments based on non-patent/publication grounds (public use, on-sale, abandonment under 35 U.S.C. 102(b)/(c)) are improper for reexamination and should be noted as such.

rubrics_metrics.name: Second or subsequent request for reexamination (multiple requests policy)
rubrics_metrics.description: A second or subsequent request for reexamination should be denied if it raises the same question of patentability as that raised in the pending reexamination proceedings.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: However, a second/subsequent request may raise an SNQ with respect to any new or amended claim proposed under 37 CFR 1.530(d) in the pending reexamination, to permit examination of the entire patent package. Prevents parties from waiting until a certificate issues to challenge amended claims and prevents patent owners from nominally amending all claims to preclude subsequent requests. In aggravated situations, after grant of a second/subsequent request, if it appears the filing was for purposes of harassment and a 37 CFR 1.182 petition by the patent owner is granted, prosecution on the second/subsequent reexamination may be suspended. The second/subsequent request should be determined on its own merits without reference to the pending reexamination.

rubrics_metrics.name: Petition to vacate an order granting reexamination (limitations)
rubrics_metrics.description: A substantive determination to institute reexamination based on an SNQ is not subject to judicial review until a final agency decision in the reexamination proceeding. There is no right to petition or request reconsideration of the SNQ finding after reexamination is granted, except in limited circumstances under 37 CFR 1.181.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A 37 CFR 1.181 petition may be filed to vacate an ultra vires reexamination order (e.g., order not based on patents/printed publications). Appropriate circumstances to vacate under 1.181(a)(3) include: (A) reexamination order not based on patents/printed publications; (B) all claims of the patent were held invalid by final federal decision after appeals; (C) reexamination ordered for wrong patent; (D) ordered based on duplicate copy of the request; (E) order based wholly on the same question of patentability raised by prior art previously considered in an earlier concluded Office examination. When such a petition is filed by a third party, the third-party requester may file a single submission in opposition, generally within two weeks of service to ensure consideration.

rubrics_metrics.name: Processing and mailing of decision and records
rubrics_metrics.description: After the examiner prepares and signs the decision, the reexamination file and decision are given to the Technology Center’s reexamination clerk for clerical processing and distribution.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Technical support staff prints the heading, prepares copies of any prior art documents not already supplied, and mails a copy of the decision to the patent owner and any third-party requester along with required prior art copies. The original signed decision and copies of any enclosed prior art are made of record in the reexamination electronic file (file history). For third-party requests, copies are provided to both patent owner and requester; if the patent owner filed the request, only a patent-owner copy is required.

rubrics_metrics.name: Handling of prior art citations submitted after the order
rubrics_metrics.description: Any prior art citations under 37 CFR 1.501 submitted after the date of the decision on the order should be retained separately and not entered immediately into the patent file.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Such submissions are stored by the Technology Center (usually the TC Special Program Examiner) until the reexamination proceeding is concluded, at which time the prior art citation is entered of record on the patent file. See MPEP § 2206.
